prompt_used:
I want to become a AI Engineer. I have 3 months to prepare and I can study 3 hours per day. 
My experience level is University Recent CSE Graduate. Need a remote job,prepare for global market, Intermediate (Built small projects) Coding experience, familiar with python, java,C++,javascript languages and familiar with Django,spring boot,.NET,tensorflow,pytorch,power BI,docker framewrok. Already done internship , preferable language is java
Now generate a learning plan for me.

generated_plan.learning_plan_title: 3-Month AI Engineer Roadmap (Java Preferred, Global Remote Market)

weeks.theme: Python for Data Science & ML Refresher
topics_and_activities: Review/Deepen NumPy & Pandas for data manipulation (6 hours)
Matplotlib/Seaborn for data visualization (3 hours)
Scikit-learn refresher: Supervised Learning algorithms (Linear/Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, SVMs, k-NN) (6 hours)
Feature Engineering & Preprocessing techniques (3 hours)
Model evaluation metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC) (3 hours)
Activity: Kaggle 'Titanic' or 'Iris' dataset classification using Scikit-learn.

weeks.theme: Supervised Learning Deep Dive & PyTorch Introduction
topics_and_activities: Ensemble methods: Random Forests, Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM concepts) (6 hours)
Cross-validation, Regularization, Hyperparameter tuning (3 hours)
Introduction to PyTorch: Tensors, Autograd, simple neural networks (6 hours)
Building a basic Feedforward Neural Network with PyTorch (6 hours)
Activity: Implement a simple neural network for MNIST classification using PyTorch.
Clustering algorithms: K-Means, DBSCAN, Hierarchical Clustering (6 hours)
Dimensionality Reduction: PCA, t-SNE (3 hours)
Working with larger datasets (e.g., efficient Pandas, Dask concepts) (6 hours)
Basic Data Pipelines & ETL concepts (using pandas/sklearn.pipeline) (6 hours)
Activity: Implement clustering on a dataset (e.g., customer segmentation).
Select a real-world dataset (e.g., housing price prediction, sentiment analysis) (3 hours)
Data collection/loading, Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) (6 hours)
Feature engineering, model selection (Scikit-learn/PyTorch) (6 hours)
Model training, evaluation, saving the model (e.g., Pickle/Joblib) (6 hours)
Activity: Complete Project 1, focusing on clean code, documentation, and a reproducible workflow.
Convolutional layers, pooling, activation functions (6 hours)
Common CNN architectures (LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet concepts) (6 hours)
Transfer Learning and Fine-tuning with pre-trained models (6 hours)
Data augmentation techniques for images (3 hours)
Activity: Image classification project using a pre-trained CNN (e.g., PyTorchvision models on CIFAR-10).

weeks.theme: Deep Learning Architectures - RNNs & NLP Basics
topics_and_activities: Recurrent layers (RNN, LSTM, GRU) (6 hours)
Sequence processing, Embeddings (Word2Vec, GloVe basics) (6 hours)
Introduction to Transformers (attention mechanism - high level concepts) (3 hours)
Basic NLP tasks: text classification, sentiment analysis (6 hours)
Activity: Sentiment analysis project using an RNN/LSTM on a text dataset.
MLOps lifecycle: Data, Model, Code, Infrastructure (3 hours)
Model versioning (e.g., DVC - basic concepts) (3 hours)
Experiment tracking (e.g., MLflow - basic concepts) (6 hours)
Model serialization for deployment (e.g., ONNX introduction, TorchScript) (3 hours)
REST APIs for ML models: Flask/FastAPI basics (Python) (6 hours)
Activity: Wrap Project 1/2 (Python) in a simple Flask/FastAPI endpoint.
Cloud provider overview (choose one, e.g., AWS): EC2, S3, IAM basics (6 hours)
Docker fundamentals: Dockerfile, images, containers (6 hours)
Containerizing an ML application (Flask/FastAPI app from Week 7) (6 hours)
Introduction to model serving frameworks (e.g., TorchServe, TensorFlow Serving concepts) (3 hours)
Activity: Dockerize the Flask/FastAPI ML application. Push to Docker Hub (optional).

monthly_breakdown.month: Month 3: AI Engineering in Practice & Interview Prep

topics_and_activities: Review Spring Boot for building REST APIs (6 hours)
Integrating Python ML models with Java backend: calling Python services via REST/gRPC (6 hours)
Using ONNX Runtime (Java API) for efficient inference of ONNX-exported models (6 hours)
Considerations for serving ML models in a Java environment (JVM performance, security) (3 hours)
Activity: Create a Spring Boot application that consumes the Dockerized Python ML service or uses ONNX Runtime for inference.
Introduction to workflow orchestration: Apache Airflow (basic DAGs) or Kubeflow (concepts) (6 hours)
Monitoring ML models: data drift, model drift, performance metrics (Prometheus/Grafana concepts) (6 hours)
CI/CD for ML (MLOps pipelines): concepts, simple GitHub Actions/GitLab CI for ML tasks (3 hours)
System Design for ML applications: scalability, latency, throughput considerations (6 hours)
Activity: Outline a full MLOps pipeline for one of your projects, considering each stage.

Project 2 (Portfolio Project): Choose a slightly more complex problem. Implement it end-to-end (data, advanced model, deployment strategy). Focus on clean code, good documentation, and testing. (12 hours)
Resume/CV tailoring for AI Engineer roles: highlight ML, MLOps, Java, cloud skills (3 hours)
LinkedIn profile optimization (3 hours)
GitHub profile cleanup and showcasing projects (3 hours)
Activity: Work intensively on Project 2. Draft/refine resume and professional profiles.
Behavioral interview questions practice (3 hours)
Technical interview questions: Data Structures & Algorithms (refresh key ones, focus on Python/Java implementation) (6 hours)
ML theory questions: Deep dive on chosen algorithms, model explainability (6 hours)
System Design for ML scenarios (practice problems) & Java-specific backend questions (3 hours)
Networking: identifying target companies, reaching out, online presence (3 hours)
Activity: Mock interviews (self or with peers), LeetCode/HackerRank practice (medium level), review ML concepts.

courses_and_books: Deep Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng (Coursera) for theoretical depth
Practical Deep Learning for Coders (fast.ai) for practical PyTorch
Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow (Geron) for comprehensive overview
Spring Boot in Action or similar for Java backend development
learning_strategy: **Hands-on First:** Implement everything you learn. Coding is paramount.
**Project-Based Learning:** Every week should have a coding activity or contribute to a project.
**Read Documentation:** Learn to navigate and understand official library/framework documentation.
**Network:** Connect with other AI/ML professionals online.
**Mock Interviews:** Practice explaining your projects and solving technical problems.

important_notes: While your preference is Java, Python is currently the dominant language for core ML development. This plan integrates both, using Python for model development and Java for robust backend/service integration.
Choose ONE cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and focus on its core ML-related services (compute, storage, basic ML services).
Tailor your portfolio projects to showcase both your ML model development skills (Python) and your ability to integrate/deploy them into production-ready systems (Java, Docker, Cloud).

For remote/global roles, strong communication skills (written and verbal English) and independent problem-solving are crucial. Practice documenting your code and explaining your thought process clearly.
This is an ambitious plan; be flexible and prioritize depth in key areas (e.g., MLOps, specific deep learning architectures) over breadth if time becomes an issue.
